quizzes.title: Upper Bhadra Trial Run
quizzes.passage: The September 2026 current affairs compilation for AILET preparation opens its governance section with an item on the Upper Bhadra Project and the Bhadra River. The item reports that a successful trial run of the Upper Bhadra Project enabled water from the Bhadra Reservoir to reach Gonur Lake in Chitradurga district. During the run, the water moved through a canal that forms part of the project's route. The booklet presents the trial as the start of the project's operational phase. It also says the development fulfils a demand for reliable water supply that has existed for a long time in parts of central Karnataka. The Upper Bhadra entry is the first item on its booklet page. The Ladakh and national accounts entries also appear on that page. The page is headed September 2026 and carries the label Topic in News. A separate item on India's national accounts appears under the economy heading on the same page. The compilation groups its items under headings such as governance, economy, environment and awards. The national accounts entry says the revised series uses 2022-23 as its base year. The Ladakh entry is the second item under the governance heading on that page. Each entry is written as a short list of points beneath its heading.

questions.q: Through which canal did the trial-run water travel to Gonur Lake?
questions.explanation: The booklet names the Chitradurga Branch Canal as the route used in the trial run.

questions.q: The Upper Bhadra Project is the first irrigation project in Karnataka to receive which status from the Union Government?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the project is the first Karnataka irrigation project to receive National Project Status.

questions.q: Near which peak does the Bhadra River originate in the Western Ghats?
questions.explanation: The booklet places the origin of the Bhadra River in the Western Ghats near Gangamoola Peak.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Bhadra River flows directly into the Krishna River.
Reason (R): The Bhadra River joins the Tunga River at Koodli, near Shivamogga.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Bhadra joins the Tunga at Koodli rather than flowing directly into the Krishna, so only R is true.

questions.q:
Match List I (left) with List II (right):
I. Bhadra River originates in   ->   A. Bay of Bengal
II. Bhadra joins Tunga River at   ->   B. Krishna River
III. Tungabhadra River is a tributary of   ->   C. Koodli
IV. Krishna river system drains into   ->   D. Western Ghats
questions.explanation: The booklet links the origin to the Western Ghats, the confluence to Koodli, the Tungabhadra to the Krishna and the Krishna system to the Bay of Bengal.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Bhadra River joins the Tunga River at Koodli.
II. The Tungabhadra River is a tributary of the Godavari River.
III. The Krishna river system drains into the Bay of Bengal.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the booklet makes the Tungabhadra a tributary of the Krishna, not the Godavari.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
The Bhadra River rises in the Western Ghats.
The Tungabhadra River is formed at Gangamoola Peak.
The Krishna river system drains into the Ganga.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Only the first statement matches the booklet, since the Tungabhadra forms at Koodli and the Krishna drains into the Bay of Bengal.

quizzes.title: Upper Bhadra Project Facts
quizzes.passage: A trial run of the Upper Bhadra Project is the lead item in the governance section of the September 2026 current affairs compilation. The trial carried water from the Bhadra Reservoir to Gonur Lake, which is situated in Chitradurga district. The booklet treats this as the point at which the project begins its operational phase. The development is described as meeting a need that had been pending for a long time: a dependable water supply for parts of central Karnataka. The same governance section contains a proposal under Article 371 for Ladakh, which is listed after the Upper Bhadra item. The economy section of the same compilation carries an item on India's national accounts. The booklet page with these items is headed September 2026 and carries the label Topic in News. The Bhadra item is the first item on that page. Each item in the compilation is placed under a subject heading, and the booklet uses the heading names governance, economy, environment and awards. The Bhadra item also has a set of bullet points about the river and its course, which the compilation lists as separate points from the trial run. The compilation's economy item is set out in its own list of points, separate from the governance item.

questions.q: Through which canal did the trial-run water travel from Bhadra Reservoir to Gonur Lake? (name of canal)
questions.explanation: The booklet names the Chitradurga Branch Canal as the route for the trial run.

questions.q: The Upper Bhadra Project is the first Karnataka irrigation project to receive which status from the Union Government? (status name)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the project is the first Karnataka irrigation project to receive National Project Status.

questions.q: In which mountain range does the Bhadra River originate? (range)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Bhadra River originates in the Western Ghats.

questions.q: Near which peak does the Bhadra River originate? (peak)
questions.explanation: The booklet places the Bhadra's origin near Gangamoola Peak.

questions.q: At which place does the Bhadra River join the Tunga River? (place)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Bhadra joins the Tunga River at Koodli, near Shivamogga.

questions.q: The Tungabhadra River is a tributary of which river? (river)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the Tungabhadra River as a tributary of the Krishna River.

questions.q: Into which body of water does the Krishna river system ultimately drain? (body of water)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Krishna river system ultimately drains into the Bay of Bengal.

quizzes.title: Ladakh Constitutional Framework
quizzes.passage: The governance section of the September 2026 current affairs compilation contains an item on a proposed Special Constitutional Framework for Ladakh. The item describes the proposal as a new chapter under Article 371. According to the item, the framework is expected to give a Union Territory level institution powers over matters that are particularly important to the region. The item also notes that other areas of legislative authority applicable to Union Territories may form part of the proposal. The Upper Bhadra Project item appears first in the same governance section. The national accounts item appears under the economy heading on that same page. The compilation groups its items under headings such as governance, economy, environment and awards. Each entry in the compilation carries a short list of points, and the Ladakh entry follows the same pattern. The page is headed September 2026 and carries the label Topic in News. The Upper Bhadra entry reports a trial run that carried water from the Bhadra Reservoir to Gonur Lake in Chitradurga district. The national accounts entry says that the revised series uses 2022-23 as its base year. On that page, the governance entries come before the economy entry. The Ladakh entry is the second item under the governance heading.

questions.q: Which ministry proposed the new chapter under Article 371 for Ladakh?
options: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Ministry of Home Affairs proposed the new chapter.

questions.q: The proposed Union Territory level institution for Ladakh is envisaged as which type of body?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the proposal as envisaging a Directly Elected Legislative Body at Union Territory level.

questions.q: Other areas of legislative authority applicable to Union Territories under which article may also form part of the proposal?
questions.explanation: The booklet says legislative areas applicable to Union Territories under Article 240 may also form part of the proposal.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The proposed institution for Ladakh is expected to receive powers over land matters alone.
Reason (R): The expected powers include local culture, traditions and language, and forests, environment and natural resources.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet lists several expected powers beyond land, so A is false while R is true.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed among the matters the proposed institution is expected to receive powers over?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists local culture, traditions and language among the expected powers.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Ministry of Home Affairs proposed a new chapter under Article 371 for Ladakh.
II. The proposed institution would have no powers over land.
III. The proposed institution is expected to receive powers over forests and natural resources.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II contradicts the booklet, which lists land among the expected powers.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
The proposal is a new chapter under Article 371.
The proposed body would be appointed rather than directly elected.
The item names the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation as the proposer.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Only the first statement matches the booklet, since the body is described as directly elected and the Ministry of Home Affairs made the proposal.

quizzes.title: Ladakh Proposal Details
quizzes.passage: A proposal for Ladakh appears in the governance section of the September 2026 current affairs compilation. The item says that a new chapter under Article 371 would set up a Special Constitutional Framework for Ladakh. The framework is expected to include a legislative institution at the Union Territory level. The item also says that the institution's expected powers concern matters that are particularly important to the region. The item notes that other areas of legislative authority for Union Territories may also be part of the proposal. The Ladakh item is the second entry under the governance heading on its page. The economy heading on the same page carries an item on India's national accounts. The page is headed September 2026 and carries the label Topic in News. The compilation sorts its items under headings such as governance, economy, environment and awards. Each entry is written as a short list of points beneath its heading. The booklet uses the word proposed in its heading for this item. The item was printed in the September 2026 edition of the compilation, which covers news for that month. Its page number appears at the foot of the page. The text on the page is arranged in sections, one for each heading.

questions.q: Which ministry proposed the new chapter under Article 371 for Ladakh? (ministry name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Ministry of Home Affairs proposed the new chapter under Article 371.

questions.q: Other legislative areas applicable to Union Territories under which article may also form part of the proposal? (article number)
questions.explanation: The booklet names Article 240 as the source of other legislative areas for Union Territories that may join the framework.

questions.q: The proposed Union Territory level institution is envisaged as what kind of legislative body? (phrase)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes a Directly Elected Legislative Body at Union Territory level.

questions.q: Which area is listed first among the expected powers of the proposed institution? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Land and Land-related Issues first among the expected powers.

questions.q: In the item's list of expected powers, which area comes immediately after Local Culture and Traditions? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Language directly after Local Culture and Traditions.

questions.q: Which item on the same booklet page comes immediately before the Ladakh entry? (name of item)
accept: Upper Bhadra Project and Bhadra River
Upper Bhadra Project and the Bhadra River
questions.explanation: The Ladakh entry is the second governance entry, and the first is the Upper Bhadra Project item.

questions.q: Besides forests and environment, which other broad area is the last in the item's list of expected powers? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet ends its list of expected powers with Natural Resources.

quizzes.title: National Accounts Revision
quizzes.passage: The economy heading of the September 2026 current affairs compilation carries an item on India's revised national accounts methodology. The item states that the revised series was released in 2026 and that it introduces several methodological changes. The revision seeks to reflect structural changes in the economy, to use improved and newer data sources, and to update statistical methodologies. It also aims for constant-price estimates that more accurately reflect the contemporary economy. The national accounts entry is set out as a list of points, in the same format as the other entries on the page. The page is headed September 2026 and carries the label Topic in News. The governance heading above the economy entry contains the Upper Bhadra Project item. That governance section also includes the proposal for Ladakh, which follows the Upper Bhadra item. The compilation groups its items under headings such as governance, economy, environment and awards. The economy heading on this page holds only the national accounts entry. The Upper Bhadra entry reports a trial run that carried water from the Bhadra Reservoir to Gonur Lake in Chitradurga district. The next booklet page opens with an environment item on India's first Blue Bond. The booklet's running header names the AILET Corner series.

questions.q: Which ministry released India's revised National Accounts Series in 2026?
options: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation released the revised series.

questions.q: The revised series adopts which financial year as its new base year?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives 2022-23 as the new base year of the revised series.

questions.q: Which method is adopted for Manufacturing Gross Value Added in the revision?
questions.explanation: The revised series adopts double deflation for Manufacturing Gross Value Added.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): National accounts measure only the production of goods in an economy.
Reason (R): National accounts measure production, income, expenditure, consumption, investment, saving and external trade.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet lists several measures beyond production, so A is false while R is true.

questions.q: The estimates in the revised series are prepared broadly in line with which system?
options: United Nations System of National Accounts
questions.explanation: The booklet says the estimates are prepared broadly in accordance with the United Nations System of National Accounts.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The revised series uses 2022-23 as its new base year.
II. The revision was released by the Ministry of Home Affairs.
III. National accounts measure saving and external trade.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation released the revised series.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
The revision adopts double deflation for Manufacturing Gross Value Added.
The estimates are prepared broadly in line with the UN System of National Accounts.
The revision uses 2019-20 as its new base year.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The first two statements match the booklet, while the base year is 2022-23, so only two are correct.

quizzes.title: National Accounts Series Facts
quizzes.passage: The economy heading in the September 2026 current affairs compilation has a single entry on national accounts. The entry describes India's revised National Accounts Series, which was released by a government statistics ministry. The revision introduces several methodological changes, which the entry lists in a short set of points. Among its aims, the revision seeks to incorporate structural changes in the economy. It also seeks to use improved and newer data sources and to update statistical methodologies. The entry describes a systematic framework for measuring an economy's activity. The item on the Upper Bhadra Project sits under the governance heading on the same booklet page. A further governance entry on that page concerns a proposed constitutional framework for a Union Territory. The compilation groups its items under headings such as governance, economy, environment and awards. The next booklet page opens with an environment item on India's first Blue Bond. The page is headed September 2026 and carries the label Topic in News. The national accounts entry is presented as a short list of points beneath its heading. The booklet's running header names the AILET Corner series. The item on the revised series is set in the economy section of the compilation.

questions.q: Which ministry released the revised National Accounts Series? (ministry name)
questions.answer: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
accept: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation released the revised series.

questions.q: The revised series adopts which financial year as its new base year? (financial year)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives 2022-23 as the new base year.

questions.q: Which deflation method is adopted for Manufacturing Gross Value Added in the revision? (method name)
questions.explanation: The revised series adopts double deflation for Manufacturing Gross Value Added.

questions.q: Which system are the revised estimates broadly prepared in line with? (name or abbreviation)
questions.answer: United Nations System of National Accounts
questions.explanation: The booklet says the estimates are prepared broadly in line with the United Nations System of National Accounts.

questions.q: National accounts give a framework for measuring an economy's production, income, expenditure, consumption, investment, saving and one further aspect. What is that aspect? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists external trade as the final item measured by national accounts.

questions.q: Which item on the same booklet page comes immediately before the national accounts entry? (name of item)
questions.explanation: The booklet places the Ladakh proposal in the governance section directly before the economy heading and its national accounts entry.

questions.q: What term describes the estimates that more accurately reflect the contemporary economy under the revision? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the revision aims for constant-price estimates that more accurately reflect the contemporary economy.
